content.text: Four measurements so far put the peak near Sb≈0.25 (index 6). I'm using XRD to check which side of 6 has the active phase before spending the last EQE measurement.

XRD on 4, 6 and 8 was dominated by the Pt substrate reflections, so the phases could not be told apart.

content.text:
I submitted **index 6 (Sb fraction 0.247)** as the best composition. At 0.040% EQE, it was the only one of the five I measured that gave a clear photoresponse. I can't say if it's the true best on the line: the response looks very narrow, and I ran out of EQE measurements before I could check some promising neighbours.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.165 | −0.0004 |
| **6** | **0.247** | **0.040** |
| 7 | 0.270 | −0.001 |
| 13 | 0.453 | 0.0016 |
| 20 | 0.674 | 0.001 |

- **Narrow active window:** index 7 is right next to index 6 and gave essentially nothing.
- **Unmeasured neighbours:** index 5 (0.220) and index 8 (0.295) might beat index 6. The Gaussian-process model predicted index 8 at about 0.039%, which is close to index 6, but that was a prediction, not a measurement.
- **Phase not identified:** I ran XRD on indices 4, 6 and 8, but the platinum substrate's peaks dominated all three patterns. I couldn't tell which cobalt–antimony oxide phase is responsible. Index 6 lies where the cobalt-rich spinel-type phases (Co₇Sb₂O₁₂, Co₃SbO₈) sit, but that's only an inference from composition.
- **Cobalt-poor end:** the CoSb₂O₆ composition around Sb 0.67 was inactive (index 20).

I used all 5 EQE measurements and 3 of the 5 XRD measurements.
